chunks.text: 64-year-old female, Retired, resident of Choa Chu Kang, Singapore.
Uncomplicated spinal anesthesia for left cataract surgery in 2021

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Liew from the anesthesia team. Today, we'll go through some questions to prepare you for your hip replacement surgery. Let's start with why you're having this surgery. Can you tell me about your left hip problem?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, doctor. My left hip been hurting a lot for years, lah. Can't walk far, even with cane. X-ray show bad arthritis, so doctor say need to replace it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Now, let's review your medications. Your records list amlodipine, metformin, and atorvastatin. Are you still taking all these?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Amlodipine and atorvastatin still taking every day, doctor. But metformin... stopped already one year plus.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Metformin was stopped? Can you tell me why?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. My sugar level very good on diet alone. HbA1c last check was 6.2%, so doctor say can stop metformin.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I see. We'll update your records. Any allergies? Your file mentions penicillin causes a rash.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. Once take penicillin, body get red spots. Never take again after that.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Noted. Have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. Wife make sure I NPO from last night. Only sip water for meds.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Any previous surgeries or anesthesia? Any problems during those times?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Had gallbladder out ten years back. Anesthesia okay, wake up no problem. No dizziness or vomiting.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Finally, how's your mobility now? Can you walk with assistance?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Can walk short distance with cane, but pain very bad. Need help for stairs or long walks.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Tan. We'll proceed with spinal anesthesia and propofol sedation as planned. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. All clear. Thank you for explaining everything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] spinal anesthetic administered bupivacaine twenty-five milligrams with fentanyl twenty micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] propofol infusion started at fifty milligrams per hour

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] endotracheal tube placed, grade one view confirmed

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] eighteen-gauge peripheral IV line placed in left hand

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:00] one liter of normal saline administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] hypotension noted, blood pressure sixty over forty, treated with phenylephrine twenty micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi Mr Tan, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Doc, my left hip is sore, but not too bad lah. I can tolerate it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Okay, can you rate your pain on a scale of 0 to 10 for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe 4 or 5? It’s a dull pain, not sharp one.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or vomiting since waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A bit dizzy earlier, but no vomiting. Stomach feels okay now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: How’s your breathing? Any tightness or discomfort in your chest?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine, but my throat is a bit dry. Maybe from the tube during surgery?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That’s normal. Did you remember anything during the operation?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I was out cold. Only woke up when they moved me here.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any chest pain, shortness of breath, or unusual symptoms linked to your blood pressure or sugar levels?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Blood pressure been stable, no chest pain. My sugar was 7.2 this morning, so okay lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Let us know if you need more pain relief or feel unwell. Rest well, Mr Tan.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thanks, doc. I’ll let the nurse know if anything comes up.

No heart disease, respiratory symptoms, or diabetes complications reported. Gallbladder surgery 10 years ago without anesthesia issues. NPO since midnight.

Monitor blood pressure closely, continue fluid resuscitation as needed, resume home medications (amlodipine, atorvastatin), and assess for delayed respiratory or cardiovascular complications.

64-year-old female with history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, osteoarthritis (left hip), resolved pneumonia (2018), right wrist fracture (2015, fully healed), and discontinued simvastatin in 2020.
Current medications include amlodipine 5mg daily and atorvastatin 20mg daily. Metformin 500mg twice daily was discontinued one year prior due to adequate glycemic control (HbA1c 6.2%).
Allergy to penicillin (rash).
Past surgeries include cholecystectomy (10 years ago) with uncomplicated anesthesia and left cataract surgery (2021) under spinal anesthesia.
Endotracheal tube placed with grade 1 view during surgery. Postoperative complaint of dry throat attributed to intraoperative intubation.
Spinal anesthesia with bupivacaine 25mg and fentanyl 20mcg, supplemented with propofol infusion at 50mg/hr.

Postoperative pain rated 4/10 (dull, non-sharp), no nausea or vomiting, transient dizziness resolved. Blood pressure stabilized after intraoperative hypotension (60/40 mmHg) treated with phenylephrine 20mcg.
No postoperative nausea or vomiting reported.
Normal respiratory effort, no chest tightness or shortness of breath. Capable of normal conversation.
No intraoperative recall or awareness reported. Patient remained asleep until emergence.
Postoperative concerns include left hip pain management and monitoring of diabetes given discontinued metformin.
